title: Database-backed tests share state while asserting an empty database
reasoning: Several tests write committed rows through the global SQLModel engine and do not clean them up, while other tests assert globally empty or first-row state. For example, the PDF download test persists a Feed, then `test_list_feeds_empty` expects `/api/feeds` to be empty in the same test database. Similarly, `test_download_digest_by_id_epub` validates `digests_response.json()[0]` instead of locating the digest it created, so stale rows can make the assertion check the wrong digest. This makes the suite order-dependent and prone to full-run failures.
reproduction: Run a database-writing test such as `tests/test_digest_download_formats.py::test_download_digest_by_id_pdf_generates_on_demand` in the same pytest session before `tests/test_feeds.py::test_list_feeds_empty`; the feed row committed by the first test remains visible to `/api/feeds`, contradicting the empty-list assertion.
recommendation: Add test database isolation, preferably an autouse fixture that clears all tables or wraps each test in a rollback transaction against a test engine. Also change list assertions to locate records by their created IDs instead of assuming index 0 belongs to the current test.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests are the affected surface; they assume isolation rather than enforcing it. Some assertions such as `>= 1` in retry tests tolerate leaked state, which masks the same root cause instead of proving clean setup.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an isolation check that creates a feed in one test and verifies a subsequent test starts from an empty database, or enable randomized test ordering in CI after adding the cleanup fixture.
minimumFixScope: Introduce shared database cleanup in the test fixture layer and adjust order-sensitive assertions in the owned tests.
